name: plato
description: An AI coding agent for VS Code that shows its work, lets you steer mid-run, and stops at a safe point.

scripts.test: node -e "console.log('no unit tests in the shell; core carries the logic')"

plato.connections.description: Named OpenAI-compatible/Anthropic connections (D26a, D43: nothing is pre-seeded). Example: [{"id":"litellm","kind":"openai","baseUrl":"http://localhost:4000/v1","models":["gpt-4o"]}]

id.description: Connection id used in model refs, e.g. litellm

models.description: The models this connection offers, in this order. Written by Fetch models; every entry is selectable. Omit only if the connection has never been fetched.

plato.model.description: Default model as connection:model (e.g. litellm:gpt-4o). The header dropdown overrides this per chat.

plato.reasoning.description: Reasoning effort for models that support it (o4-mini, Claude extended thinking). Ignored otherwise.

plato.orchestration.description: Orchestration mode: solo = Plato alone; duo = Plato + one philosopher; academy = Plato + the council defined in ACADEMY.yaml.

plato.compaction.threshold.description: D44d: fraction of the model's context window at which auto-compaction triggers (0.5–0.95, default 0.8). Compaction is always auto at this threshold; /compact (or the ring's Compact-now) forces it on demand.

plato.secrets.protect.markdownDescription: D49bb: extra file names to protect, on top of the built-in list (`keystore.properties`, `local.properties`, `.env*`, `*.keystore`, `*.jks`, `secrets.*`). A name matches the file's last path segment, and `*` is allowed at the start or the end (`*.pem`). Plato never sends a protected file's values to a model: it shows the file with each value replaced by a placeholder.

plato.secrets.allow.markdownDescription: D49bb: exact workspace-relative paths to take OFF the protected list, so Plato shows them in full. Use this for a file that matches a built-in name but holds no secret in this project, for example `local.properties` or `.env.example`. One path per entry, from the workspace root.

plato.search.respectGitignore.markdownDescription: Skip the files that your `.gitignore` file lists when Plato searches. **Off by default.** When off, Plato searches all files and marks the files that `.gitignore` lists. When on, Plato does not search these files. A file that you name is always read and edited. A change applies to the next run.
